n8b6017ea616.s: The five countries that together hold more than 54% of the world's forests are:
o: India, Brazil, Canada, Australia and China
Brazil, Canada, Australia, India and the United States
Russia, Brazil, Canada, the United States and China
Russia, India, the United States, Indonesia and China
n8b6017ea616.x: Russia, Brazil, Canada, the United States and China together hold more than 54% of the world's forests.

n0bd7f00771d.s: Which of the following contributes to the formation of urban heat islands?
n0bd7f00771d.x: Loss of vegetation is a cause of urban heat islands, alongside heat-storing low-albedo concrete and asphalt; cool roofs and urban forests counter them.

na6840d730df.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the UNCCD?
o: It was adopted in 1994 in Paris
Its secretariat is located in Bonn
India is a party to the Convention
na6840d730df.x: The UNCCD was adopted in Paris in 1994 but entered into force only in 1996; its secretariat is in Bonn and India is a party.

n4202595697b.s: UNCCD COP17, where India's first guide to Grasslands and Open Natural Ecosystems was launched, was held at:
n4202595697b.x: COP17 (2026) was held at Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia; New Delhi hosted COP14 in 2019.

ne35ff530d3a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Boards under the Air Act, 1981?
o: The CPCB was originally set up under the Water Act
The Air Act created an entirely separate set of Boards unrelated to the Water Act
The existing CPCB was assigned air-pollution functions
The SPCBs enforce the Air Act in the States
ne35ff530d3a.x: The Air Act used the same Boards: the CPCB, set up under the Water Act, got air functions and SPCBs enforce it in States.

n83db792b67d.s: Under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the power to regulate the location of industries rests with the:
n83db792b67d.x: The Centre's powers under the Act include regulating the location of industries, besides standards, hazardous waste and public health.

n323623f2ca3.s: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 amended the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991, penalty rates are specified in the:
n323623f2ca3.x: The amendment replaced imprisonment with penalties and shifted penalty rates from the Act to the rules.

n4ad93d30a6c.s: In Vanashakti v. Union of India, ex post facto environmental clearance was held possible only through:
o: Payment of a penalty, in every case
An administrative order overriding the EIA Notification, 2006
n4ad93d30a6c.x: Ex post facto clearance is not available merely on payment of a penalty; Article 142 may be applied only in fit cases.

nenvironment-5-13.s: The background event of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was the:
nenvironment-5-13.x: The Bhopal gas tragedy (1984) was the background to the EPA, popularly called umbrella legislation.

nb9545e34da2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about notifications under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986?
o: Doon Valley (1989) barred industries burning over 24 MT of coal/fuel a day
Revdanda Creek (1989) barred industries around the creek
Revdanda Creek (1989) declared the area ecologically fragile and barred power plants
Dhanu Taluka (1991) was declared ecologically fragile with no power plants
nb9545e34da2.x: Revdanda Creek barred industries around the creek; the 'ecologically fragile, no power plants' rule belongs to Dhanu Taluka (1991).

o: Praised for longer public consultation periods than 2006
Notable for abolishing penalties for violations
Not finalised, and criticised for proposing post-facto clearance
n61230b85bad.x: The 2020 draft was not finalised and was contested, particularly for post-facto clearance and shorter consultation periods.

n145a4925e61.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about EIA project categories?
o: Category B projects are appraised by the central Expert Appraisal Committee
Category B projects are cleared by SEIAA
Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC
Category A projects are cleared by MoEFCC
n145a4925e61.x: Category B projects are appraised by the State Expert Appraisal Committee and cleared by SEIAA; the central EAC appraises Category A.

n861ec154597.s: The EIA Notification, 2006 made environmental clearance compulsory for how many project categories?
n861ec154597.x: The 2006 notification made environmental clearance compulsory for 39 project categories.

n3f26d74883e.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, a public hearing must be completed within:
n3f26d74883e.x: The hearing notice must be given at least 30 days in advance and the hearing completed within 45 days.

nb11d8ce000c.s: Under the Draft EIA Notification, 2020, violations could be reported only by:
nb11d8ce000c.x: The draft restricted reporting of violations to the violator or the government, one of its contested provisions.

n29ad4bd69fd.s: Under the 2026 backup arrangement for environmental appraisal bodies, which body stands in for SEIAA?
n29ad4bd69fd.x: SAEIA is the backup for SEIAA, while SCEIA is the backup for SEAC.

n65c65f473c0.s: A major criticism of EIA reports in India is that they are often prepared by:
o: Consultants paid by the project proponents
n65c65f473c0.x: EIA reports are often prepared by proponent-paid consultants; another criticism is the lack of a central baseline data bank.

n48c4bb7a99e.s: Which case examined the 2020 exemption for extraction of ordinary earth for linear projects?
n48c4bb7a99e.x: Noble M. Paikada examined the 2020 ordinary-earth exemption; Common Cause concerned Odisha mining beyond environmental clearance.

nf7792a17069.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Alembic Pharmaceuticals v. Rohit Prajapati?
o: The 2002 MoEF circular permitting such clearance was quashed
The Court directed closure of every project concerned
Ex post facto clearance was held contrary to the EIA regime
nf7792a17069.x: The Court imposed compensation instead of ordering closure of every project.

new.s: Garrett Hardin propounded the 'Tragedy of the Commons' in:
new.x: Hardin's Tragedy of the Commons (1968) describes how over-use of a shared pasture lowers land quality.

new.s: Land Degradation Neutrality under SDG 15.3 is to be achieved by:
new.x: LDN means no net loss of land health by 2030 (SDG 15.3).

new.s: In 70 years, the organic carbon content of Indian soils fell from about 1% to:
new.x: Soil organic carbon in Indian soils fell from 1% to 0.3% in 70 years.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (resource depletion – cause) is correctly matched?
new.x: Groundwater is depleted by over-irrigation; topsoil by erosion from overgrazing and deforestation, habitats by deforestation, land by salinity and waterlogging.

new.s: By 2050, salinisation and waterlogging could affect about what share of the world's arable land?
new.x: Salinisation and waterlogging from over-irrigation and poor drainage could affect 50% of world arable land by 2050.

new.s: Removal of a thin, even layer of topsoil over a wide area is called:
new.x: Sheet erosion removes a thin even layer of topsoil; rills are small channels and gullies deep channels.

new.s: Deep gully channels in the Chambal basin are known as:
new.x: Gully erosion in clayey soil creates badlands, called ravines in the Chambal basin.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (conservation method – how it works) is correctly matched?
o: Strip cropping – steps cut on slopes
Shelter belts – grass strips between crops
Contour ploughing – ploughing along contours slows water down slopes
new.x: Contour ploughing slows water down slopes; terracing cuts steps, strip cropping uses grass strips and shelter belts are tree windbreaks.

new.s: Shelter belts have helped stabilise sand dunes in which part of India?
new.x: Shelter belts are tree rows used as windbreaks; they stabilised dunes in western India.

new.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
new.x: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan, on 19 February 2015.

new.s: Under the Soil Health Card scheme, a card is issued to farmers once every:
new.x: A Soil Health Card is issued every 2 years.

new.s: As per FAO FRA 2025, the only region with a net gain in forest area is:
new.x: Asia, led by China and India, is the only region with a net forest gain.

new.s: As per FAO FRA 2025, annual net forest loss during 2015-2025 was about:
new.x: FRA 2025 puts net loss at 10.7 Mha/yr in the 1990s falling to 4.12 Mha/yr in 2015-2025; 8.3 to 5.2 is the older FRA.

new.s: As per FAO FRA 2025, India ranks ____ in the world in forest area.
new.x: India is 9th in forest area (10th in 2020) and 3rd in annual forest gain.

new.s: As per the India State of Forest Report 2023, India's forest and tree cover together is:
new.x: Forest plus tree cover is 25.17% (forest 21.76%, tree 3.41%).

new.s: As per ISFR 2023, which State recorded the largest loss of forest cover?
new.x: Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka had the largest losses; Chhattisgarh, UP and Odisha were among the top gainers.

new.s: As per ISFR 2023, which State recorded the highest gain in forest and tree cover?
new.x: Chhattisgarh led the gains, followed by Uttar Pradesh, Odisha and Rajasthan.

new.s: Which State has over 23% of India's desertified land?
new.x: Rajasthan has over 23% of India's desertified land.

new.s: As per the Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas 2021, what share of India's area is degraded?
new.x: About 97.85 Mha, or 29.77% of India, is degraded; 33.81% is Andhra Pradesh's figure.

new.s: The main contributors to land degradation in India, as per the Atlas 2021, are:
o: Waterlogging and wind erosion of dunes
new.x: The Atlas identifies water erosion and chemical degradation as the main contributors.

new.s: Which Indian region is notably affected by sand and dust storms?
new.x: Sand and dust storms hit NW India (Rajasthan), West Asia and the Sahel.

new.s: India's land-restoration target before COP14, set at Paris in 2015, was:
new.x: India raised its target from 21 Mha (Paris 2015) to 26 Mha by 2030 at COP14, New Delhi.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the UNCCD:
1. It is the only legally binding framework on desertification.
2. It is one of the three Rio conventions.
3. India ratified it in 1994.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; India ratified the UNCCD in 1996, the year it entered into force.

new.s: The Great Green Wall across Africa's Sahel belt is an initiative of the:
new.x: The Great Green Wall is led by the African Union; the Bonn Challenge was launched by Germany and IUCN.

new.s: The Bonn Challenge aims to restore how much degraded land by 2030?
new.x: The Bonn Challenge targets 150 Mha by 2020 and 350 Mha by 2030.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT covered by the Aravalli Green Wall project?
new.x: The Aravalli Green Wall covers Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi as a barrier to the Thar; Madhya Pradesh is not included.

new.s: As per MoEFCC-IUCN, which State led India's land restoration during 2011-2020?
new.x: India restored 21.76 Mha in 2011-2020; Telangana led with 4.18 Mha, followed by MP, Odisha, Gujarat and AP.

new.s: The Mitti Bachao movement of 1977 took place in:
new.x: Mitti Bachao (1977) was in Madhya Pradesh against waterlogging and salinity; Appiko was in Karnataka.

new.s: Which of the following pairs (movement – leader) is correctly matched?
new.x: Chipko (1973) was led by Chandi Prasad Bhatt and Sunderlal Bahuguna; Panduranga Hegde led Appiko (1983).

new.s: The Mitti Bachao movement protested against waterlogging and salinity caused by the:
new.x: Mitti Bachao arose around the Tawa dam in Hoshangabad, Madhya Pradesh.

new.s: India's first Heat Action Plan was prepared by which city in 2013?
new.x: Ahmedabad prepared India's first Heat Action Plan in 2013.

new.s: The NDMA issued its heat action plan guidelines in:
new.x: The NDMA issued heat action plan guidelines in 2016, after Ahmedabad's first plan in 2013.

new.s: Which measures are used against desertification in Rayalaseema?
new.x: Rayalaseema relies on ridge-to-valley watershed works, afforestation and green-wall planting; straw checkerboards belong to China's Three-North programme.

new.s: As per the SDG India Index 2023-24, the State with the least degraded land is:
new.x: Punjab has the least degraded land at 3.15%, against Andhra Pradesh's 33.81%.

new.s: In Andhra Pradesh, fallow land, which exceeds the forest area, is about:
new.x: AP's fallow land is 21.26% (34.65 lakh ha), more than its forest cover of 18.28%.

new.s:
Arrange the following Acts in chronological order:
1. Forest (Conservation) Act
2. Water (P&CP) Cess Act
3. Air (P&CP) Act
4. Public Liability Insurance Act
new.x: Water Cess Act 1977, Forest (Conservation) Act 1980, Air Act 1981 and PLI Act 1991.

new.s: The Biological Diversity Act was enacted in:
new.x: The Biological Diversity Act came in 2002, between the PLI Act (1991) and the NGT Act (2010).

new.s: Articles 48A and 51A(g) were inserted into the Constitution by the:
new.x: Both Articles were inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

new.s: Courts have read the right to a clean and healthy environment into:
new.x: Article 21 (right to life) has been read to include a clean and healthy environment.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about constitutional provisions on the environment?
o: Article 48A is a Directive Principle addressed to the State
Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty of citizens
Article 253 is the basis of the EP Act, 1986
Article 48A is a Fundamental Duty of citizens
new.x: Article 48A is a DPSP placing the duty on the State; the citizen's duty is in Article 51A(g).

new.s: The Water Act, 1974 has:
new.x: The Water Act has 8 chapters and 64 sections; the Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections.

new.s: Proceeds of the Water Cess are credited to the:
new.x: Water Cess goes to the Consolidated Fund of India; the EP Fund is kept in the Public Account.

new.s: Which Section of the Water Act, 1974 empowers directions including environmental compensation?
new.x: Section 33A of the Water Act provides for directions; Section 31A is the Air Act equivalent.

new.s: The Air Act, 1981 came into force on:
new.x: The Air Act was enacted on 29 March 1981 and came into force on 16 May 1981.

new.s: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981 has:
new.x: The Air Act has 7 chapters and 54 sections, against the Water Act's 8 chapters and 64 sections.

new.s: Which Section of the EP Act, 1986 empowers the Centre to issue directions, including closure of industries?
new.x: Section 5 provides for directions including closure; Section 3(3) is for authorities and Section 16 the EP Fund.

new.s: Money in the Environment Protection Fund is shared between States/UTs and the Centre in the ratio:
new.x: The EP Fund gives 75% to States/UTs and 25% to the Centre.

new.s: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 is popularly called:
new.x: The EPA is umbrella legislation, coordinating authorities under the Water and Air Acts.

new.s: The Green Credit Rules under the EP Act were notified in:
new.x: The Green Credit Rules (2023) reward voluntary tree planting on degraded land.

new.s: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, appeals against penalties under the EP Act lie to the:
new.x: Penalties are fixed by an adjudicating officer and appeals go to the NGT.

new.s: After the Jan Vishwas Act, 2023, monetary penalties under the EP Act are fixed by:
new.x: The Act decriminalised the EPA penalty regime; an adjudicating officer fixes penalties.

new.s: The Jan Vishwas amendment raised relief for death under the PLI Act, 1991 from Rs 25,000 to:
new.x: Relief for death was raised from Rs 25,000 to Rs 5 lakh.

new.s: The Ministry of Environment and Forests was renamed MoEFCC in:
new.x: Department of Environment 1980, Ministry of Environment and Forests 1985, MoEFCC 2014.

new.s: The CPCB was constituted in September 1974 under the:
new.x: The CPCB was set up under the Water Act in 1974, before the Air Act (1981) existed.

new.s: The National Clean Air Programme (2019) covers how many cities?
new.x: NCAP covers 130 cities in 24 States/UTs.

new.s: The online consent system of the AP Pollution Control Board is called:
new.x: APPCB uses OCMMS (Online Consent Management and Monitoring System) for faster, transparent consents.

new.s: Besides its head office at Vijayawada, the AP Pollution Control Board has:
new.x: APPCB has its head office at Vijayawada with 3 Zonal and 13 Regional offices.

new.s: Which CPCB category of industries is practically non-polluting and needs no consent?
new.x: White (pollution index 20 or less) needs no consent; Blue is for essential environmental services.

new.s: Consent to Establish (CTE) from the SPCB must be obtained:
new.x: CTE is taken before setting up; Consent to Operate (CTO) is taken before production.

new.s: The principle of absolute liability was laid down in which case?
o: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum gas leak)
new.x: Absolute liability came from the Oleum gas leak case (Shriram plant, Delhi, 1985).

new.s: The Supreme Court first applied the polluter pays principle in:
o: M.K. Ranjitsinh v. Union of India
new.x: The Bichhri (Udaipur) H-acid sludge case, ICELA 1996, was the first SC application of polluter pays.

new.s: The precautionary principle was upheld in which case concerning tanneries?
new.x: Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum (1996) concerned tanneries and held both principles part of the law of the land.

new.s: In M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath, the public trust doctrine was applied to a motel on the river:
new.x: The case concerned a motel on the Beas; the lease was quashed under the public trust doctrine.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Oleum gas leak case:
1. It laid down the principle of absolute liability.
2. It concerned the Shriram plant in Delhi.
3. It applied the public trust doctrine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Oleum case (1985) laid down absolute liability for the Shriram plant leak; public trust was applied in M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath.

new.s: EIA was first used in India in:
new.x: EIA was first used in 1978, after the 1976-77 DST review of river-valley projects.

new.s: The R2 Code of Practices relates to:
new.x: R2 Code of Practices is not EIA; it is for responsible electronics recycling.

new.s: Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA) focuses on:
o: A specific project before it starts
A product or process from cradle to grave
new.x: LCA covers a product's life cycle; EIA covers a project, SEA policies and an audit a running unit.

new.s: Checking the compliance of a running unit after the fact is done through:
new.x: An environmental audit assesses compliance of a running unit after the fact.

new.s: The combined effect of several projects in one area is assessed through:
new.x: Cumulative Impact Assessment examines the combined effect of several projects in one area.

new.s: At which EIA stage does an expert committee review the EIA report?
new.x: In appraisal an expert committee reviews the EIA report; screening comes first and scoping sets the Terms of Reference.

new.s: Implementation of the Environment Management Plan is checked at which EIA stage?
new.x: Monitoring, the last stage, checks implementation of the EMP.

new.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, Category A projects are cleared by:
new.x: Category A projects are appraised by the central EAC and cleared by MoEFCC.

new.s: Under the EIA Notification, 1994, projects needing MoEF clearance were listed in:
new.x: Under the 1994 notification, Schedule I projects needed MoEF clearance.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT exempt from an EIA public hearing?
new.x: Defence, strategic, B2 and industrial-estate units are exempt; Category A projects are not.

new.s: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, the minimum notice for a public hearing is:
new.x: Notice must be at least 30 days; the 2020 draft proposed cutting it to 20 days.

new.s: The PARIVESH single-window clearance portal was launched in:
new.x: PARIVESH (2018) handles environment, forest, wildlife and CRZ clearances online.

new.s: Members of the appraisal committees (EAC/SEAC) have an upper age limit of:
new.x: Members serve 3-4 years, at most two terms, with an age limit of 70.

new.s: The final Vanashakti verdict of 29 July 2026 was delivered by the bench of CJI:
new.x: The CJI Surya Kant bench prospectively nullified the 2021 OM.

new.s: The National Green Tribunal Act came into force on 18 October:
new.x: The NGT Act 2010 came into force on 18 October 2010.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a place of sitting of the National Green Tribunal?
new.x: NGT sits at New Delhi (principal), Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai; Mumbai is not a seat.

new.s: The principal seat of the National Green Tribunal is at:
new.x: The principal seat is New Delhi; Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai are other sittings.

new.s: An appeal against an NGT order lies to the Supreme Court within:
new.x: Appeals go to the Supreme Court within 90 days.

new.s: The NGT aims to dispose of cases within:
new.x: The NGT aims to dispose of cases within 6 months.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the NGT and the CPCB:
1. The NGT is a judicial tribunal.
2. The CPCB is a statutory regulator under the Water Act, 1974.
3. The CPCB can issue binding directions to the NGT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; it is the NGT that can direct the CPCB, not the reverse.

new.s: The National Environment Appellate Authority Act, which heard appeals against clearances, was enacted in:
new.x: The NEAA Act was enacted in 1997; the National Environment Tribunal Act in 1995.

new.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 and the NEAA Act, 1997 were repealed by which Section of the NGT Act?
new.x: Section 38 of the NGT Act repealed both; pending NEAA cases moved to the NGT.

new.s: The National Environment Tribunal Act, 1995 dealt with:
new.x: The NET Act 1995 covered hazardous-substance accidents; the NEAA Act 1997 covered appeals against clearances.

new.s: In 2014, the NGT banned which practice in Meghalaya?
new.x: The NGT banned rat-hole mining in Meghalaya in 2014.

new.s: In 2022, the NGT fined which States for waste mismanagement?
new.x: The NGT fined Maharashtra and West Bengal in 2022 for waste mismanagement.

new.s: In November 2017, the NGT held the Amaravati capital project to fall under:
new.x: The NGT refused to set aside the 2015 EC, held Amaravati Category B and added supervisory and implementation committees.

new.s: Which State sought a review of the Polavaram project's EIA in the Supreme Court?
new.x: Telangana sought an EIA review of Polavaram (APPSC 2018); submergence affects Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
